summary:
Round 10, doc-only, and I confirm the two things I am obliged to confirm before anything else. NO ASSERTION WAS WEAKENED: the only staged file under any test path is format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventGrantTest.java and its diff touches the class javadoc and the text inside one .as(...) description; every predicate is byte-identical, including .contains("byteStart=4096") and .contains("byteLen=65536"), for the fifth round running. And my round-9 findings are both closed as described: the K = 64 case is present and names the coalesce survivor with its ~131,072-byte gap; the M5.45h collision is resolved by drawing the sharing/shape axis rather than by loosening M5.45h, which is the resolution I said was the only admissible one -- and I checked the redrawn axis does not quietly give M5.45h back the .distinct() collapse, because a per-run implementation is 64 fetch OPERATIONS at K = 64, not one, under either wording.

CRITERION 2 DOES NOT HOLD. It breaks a ninth time, on two independent limbs, and neither is a wording preference -- both are arithmetic on the figures the cell itself records.

LIMB A, THE ONE I AM ASKED ABOUT DIRECTLY: the K = 64 case does NOT close the region below the crossover. It closes exactly one coalescer -- the 64 KiB one I happened to name last round. The interleave gap is objLen/K, so it is LARGEST at SMALLEST K: any gap-limited coalescer with GAP_LIMIT > 131,072 merges everything at K = 64 and is green at every enumerated case, while issuing K+1 requests for every K below objLen/GAP_LIMIT. At a conventional 256 KiB limit that is 32 requests against 1 at K = 31; at 1 MiB, 8 against 1 at K = 7. No byte clause can catch it, because K exact slices fetch header + sum(byteLen) exactly, which is the MINIMUM possible -- the only instrument is the request count, and no case below K = 64 has one. The row's own motivating share, 'the catch-up node holding ONE run of 1,600', sits inside the surviving region. Pinning a number pins a coalescer; the durable form is K-independence.

LIMB B, NEW AND INDEPENDENT: the bytes-bounded-above clause is stated over the SUM of byteLen while the implementation the same sentence MANDATES fetches the SPAN. At K = crossover the cell's own model puts the union span at objLen*(K-1)/(K+1) = 8,289,919 bytes, against sum(byteLen) = 169*5,243 = 886,067. So the one union slice exceeds header + sum + C unless C >= 7,403,852 (7,794,653 to also admit K = 64). Either C is KiB-scale, which is what 'a stated constant' reads as -- and criterion 2 reds its own mandated implementation at the very case it mandates, which this cell elsewhere calls worse than a loose criterion because it looks strict -- or C is ~93% of the object, at which point the bound is 2.1% tighter than 'strictly fewer bytes', the clause it exists to strengthen. The clause cannot bind and admit the intended reader at the same time.

No other surviving implementation. I re-attacked the round-trip clause (symmetric predicate, false for both sequential orders -- holds), the codec clause (non-CODEC_NONE flag plus read-and-refuse, with the GoldenSegmentV1Test fixture route named -- holds), 3b (extent disagreement refuses, and the CRC argument for why it fails silently is correct -- holds), the K = crossover + 1 and ~400 whole-object arms (exactly one request and exactly the whole-object bytes kills both single-sided threshold flips -- holds), and the total-at-the-seam clause against the fetchDirectory/fetchRange split (holds). The defect is confined to the low side of the bounded region and to the byte bound's unit.

findings.title: K = 64 pins one coalescer, not the region: the interleave gap is objLen/K and is LARGEST at SMALLEST K, so any GAP_LIMIT above 131,072 bytes survives every enumerated case and issues K+1 requests everywhere below objLen/GAP_LIMIT -- 32 against 1 at K = 31 for a 256 KiB limit
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION, the same natural one as last round with one constant changed. Correct code is `if (nodeRunCount <= crossover) { header + unionSlice(ranges) } else { wholeObjectGet() }`. The mutation is `unionSlice(ranges)` -> `coalesce(ranges, GAP_LIMIT)`, one GET per coalesced group, which is literally what doc 10 section 7 prescribes. Last round GAP_LIMIT was 64 KiB and K = 64 kills it. Set GAP_LIMIT = 256 KiB -- equally conventional, and no less so than 64 KiB, since doc 10 section 7 gives no number and the tree holds none. Walk every enumerated case with the cell's own model: 1,600 runs over 8,388,608 bytes is ~5,243 bytes per run, K runs interleaved by (indexId, partitionId) sit a gap of ~objLen/K apart, and the union spans objLen*(K-1)/(K+1). (i) K = 64: gap = 8,388,608/64 = 131,072 < 262,144, so EVERYTHING MERGES -- exactly two requests, bytes 78,400 + 8,130,205 = 8,208,605 < 8,388,608, bounded path taken, whichever relation the K = 64 case states is satisfied. GREEN. (ii) K = crossover = 169: gap = 49,637, merges, two requests, 8,368,319 bytes, fewer than whole-object by 20,289. GREEN. (iii) K = 170 and K ~ 400: whole-object arm, one request, exactly the whole-object bytes. GREEN. (iv) Criterion 1's derivedFrom: the threshold IS the recorded crossover, so a price change still moves it. GREEN. (v) The round-trip clause: both requests still issued before either response. GREEN. (vi) The codec, 3b and total-at-the-seam clauses are untouched. GREEN. Now K = 31: gap = 270,600 > 262,144, NOTHING merges, and the reader issues 32 requests against the whole-object GET's 1. K = 16: 17 against 1. That is runs-per-node scaling, which non-negotiable 6 forbids by name, switched off just below the lowest share anyone asserts -- the identical defect shape as round 9, moved 105 units down the axis rather than closed. WHY NO BYTE CLAUSE BACKSTOPS IT: K exact slices fetch header + sum(byteLen) EXACTLY, which is the minimum any implementation can fetch, so 'strictly fewer bytes' and 'bounded above' are both maximally green at every K in the surviving region. The request count is the only instrument, and the lowest K carrying one is 64. AND THE DIRECTION IS THE POINT: gap = objLen/K means the hostile end of [1, crossover) is the SMALL-K end, which is also the share the row exists for ('the catch-up node holding ONE run of 1,600, fetching 8 MiB for 5.2 KiB'). K = 64 is the mildest point in the region, not the sharpest. SECOND LIMB, CHEAPER STILL: the clause obliges only 'a case at K = 64 saying which path runs there', while the two-sided RELATIONS are stated 'AT TWO SHARES' -- the boundary pair. Read literally, a K = 64 case asserting only that the bounded path runs (fewer bytes than whole-object) greens even the 64 KiB coalescer this round was written to kill: at K = 64 it takes the bounded path and fetches header + sum = 413,952 bytes, far fewer, while issuing 65 requests. REPAIR, and it costs no extra case: put the low case at the SMALLEST bounded share -- K = 2 or K = 3, where the gap is ~2.8-4.2 MB and no coalescing limit short of the object itself merges it -- and state the same two-sided relation there (exactly TWO requests and fewer bytes than the whole-object GET). Better still, state the property in the form that survives the next edit to the crossover number: THE SLICE REQUEST COUNT IS THE SAME AT THE SMALLEST AND THE LARGEST BOUNDED SHARE, i.e. independent of K. A named K pins a constant; K-independence pins the shape, which is what 'AT EVERY K' already says and what no case currently asserts.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'AND BYTES ARE BOUNDED ABOVE, NOT ONLY "STRICTLY FEWER": at most the header range plus the sum of byteLen plus a stated constant'), against the same criterion's 'the header range and ONE UNION SLICE' and the crossover model at the same line
findings.title: The byte upper bound is expressed in the SUM of the extents while the implementation the same sentence mandates fetches their SPAN; at K = crossover the span exceeds the sum by 7,403,852 bytes, so either the clause reds the mandated reader or its constant is 93% of the object and it is weaker than the 'strictly fewer' it exists to strengthen
findings.failure_scenario: ARITHMETIC, entirely on figures this cell records. The mandated bounded path is 'the header range and ONE UNION SLICE'. The cell's own interleave model puts the union at objLen*(K-1)/(K+1), and round 9's own verdict uses the same model. At K = crossover = 169: union span = 8,388,608*168/170 = 8,289,919, plus the 78,400-byte header range = 8,368,319 bytes fetched. The bound permits 78,400 + sum(byteLen) + C = 78,400 + 169*5,243 + C = 964,467 + C. So the MANDATED implementation requires C >= 7,403,852; adding the K = 64 case requires C >= 8,130,205 - 335,552 = 7,794,653. Two horns, both bad. HORN 1 -- C is KiB-scale, which is the only thing 'a stated constant' reads as next to a 78,400-byte header range: criterion 2 then REDS ITS OWN MANDATED IMPLEMENTATION at the very case it mandates, the union slice at K = crossover, and the owner's compliant options are the two the cell already names as wrong -- the removal arm chosen on a wording artifact, or per-run slices, which fetch exactly sum(byteLen) and are the ONLY shape that satisfies a tight bound (and are Limb A's 170-against-1). This cell states the rule against itself: 'A criterion that reds the intended implementation is worse than a loose one, because it looks strict.' HORN 2 -- C is set to 7,794,653 so the mandated reader is legal: the bound then permits 8,208,605 bytes at K = 64 against a whole-object 8,388,608, i.e. it is 2.1% tighter than 'strictly fewer bytes', which is the clause it was added to strengthen ('NOT ONLY "STRICTLY FEWER"'). At that C a constant of 93% of the object is doing all the work and the bound has no content of its own. The named survivor it was written to kill also comes back in most of the region: an open-ended `bytes=byteStart-` is bounded by objLen - min(byteStart), which at every K where the first wanted run is not near the head sits under 964,467 + 7,794,653. REPAIR: bound on the SPAN, not the sum -- at most the header range plus (max(byteStart + byteLen) - min(byteStart)) plus a stated constant. That admits the union slice at every K by construction, keeps C at KiB scale where it belongs, and still kills the open-ended suffix, which exceeds the span by objLen - max(byteStart + byteLen) -- at K = 2 the span is ~2.80 MB and the suffix ~5.59 MB, a factor of two clear. Note this is not the finding round 9 raised: that one checked the suffix against 'strictly fewer' at K = 169 and found it red there. The bounded-above clause has never been checked against the union it sits in the same sentence as.
